body: When two objects at different temperatures make thermal contact, energy tends to move from the warmer object to the cooler one. This transfer due to a temperature difference is called heat. A temperature describes the thermal condition of a system. A large and a small volume of the same liquid can share a temperature while containing different amounts of internal energy.

A phase is a form of matter with uniform physical properties. Ice and liquid water are different phases that can coexist during melting. Whether a substance is solid, liquid or gas can depend on both temperature and pressure. Boiling begins when the vapor pressure of the liquid reaches the surrounding pressure.

limitations: These examples describe familiar materials close to thermal equilibrium. Temperature alone cannot determine the phase without additional conditions.
purpose: Separate temperature, heat transfer and stored internal energy.
